checks.comparison: Planned SmoothObjective f L means: HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x for every x (differentiability) and ||gradient f x - gradient f y|| <= L||x - y|| for all x, y. This is Assumption 1.1. L > 0 is in valid, as the accepted graph interpretation requires.
SmoothObjective has nothing beyond differentiability with gradient and the Lipschitz bound. Using gradient f on Point d = EuclideanSpace R (Fin d) is the standard reading of grad f on R^d.
LowerBounded f lower (forall x, lower <= f x). Instance.lower plays the role of f^*. Assumption 1.2 is covered.
Nothing is added. Any lower bound may serve as f^*, as in the source wording "there exist f^*".

Reused LongTails IsStochasticGradient mu f g sigma (inspected in LongTails/Setups/StochasticSmoothAndConvex.lean). It has fields measurable (uncurry g), integrable (g x), unbiased (integral of g x = gradient f x) and the variance fields, applied to the hidden sample law mu.
The measurable and integrable fields are the implicit conditions already accepted in the graph (A3 interpretation). No moment bound is added beyond the source.
IsStochasticGradient.variance gives integral of ||g x - gradient f x||^2 dmu <= sigma^2 for all x, and 0 <= sigma is in valid. This is Assumption 1.3.
variance_integrable only makes the source integral meaningful. Taking sigma >= 0 with sigma^2 in the bound is equivalent to the source sigma^2 >= 0.

Tree (base, point, grad : N -> N, WellFormed: all <= j) together with Hist.step / Tree.realize implements Algorithm 1. At step j node j+1 = node(base j) - gamma * (reply of call grad j). Call j evaluates g at node(point j) with tape sample eta^j. V starts as {w^0 = x0}.

Each call is one evaluation g(w_grad; eta), as in Algorithm 1. Gradient reuse goes through grad j < j (the accepted ALG interpretation). The fixed tree is a public parameter (the accepted fixed-structure interpretation). All tape coordinates have law mu, which is eta ~ D_xi. Nothing else is added.

SampleIndependent T m gamma x0 g P: for every k, eta(auxSample k) is IndepFun under P of the tuple (x^{i+1}, z^{i+1}, xi^i)_{i<k} built from Tree.vertex. The tuple and quantifier are exactly those of Condition 1. It is required in admissible at the tuned step stepSize L sigma eps R, the step actually run.
There is no IID or product-law requirement on P beyond the marginals, which the plan states explicitly. Condition 1 is stated for the realised vectors of the actual run, as in the source.
ReprContained T m: forall k, T.repr(auxNode m k) <= T.repr(m k) as multisets of call indices. This is Condition 2 under the accepted identification of gradients by computation.
Multiset <= is the source meaning (proof uses uplus). Nothing is added.
DistanceBounded T m R: forall k, (dist(m k, auxNode m k) : R) <= R, with 0 <= R in valid. This is Condition 3 with finite R, as accepted in the graph.
Nothing beyond the accepted finite-R interpretation.

IsMainBranch m: m 0 = 0, and 0 < m(k+1) with base(m(k+1)-1) = m k (node m(k+1) is a child of node m k). auxSample m k = grad(m(k+1)-1) is the call whose gradient weights the edge; auxNode = point of that call is z^k; xi^k = eta(auxSample k). This matches Def. 2.1.
Indices are the node-creation order of Algorithm 1. Uniqueness of (z^k, xi^k) holds by construction. No addition.

Tree.depth, Tree.ancestors (root path including the node) and dist y z = max(depth y - D, depth z - D), where D is the sup of depth over common ancestors. Ancestor sets are chains, so D is the depth of the closest common ancestor. This is Def. 2.2.
dist(x, x) = 0 and the example dist(w^9, w^4) = 4 are reproduced. No addition.
Tree.repr j = multiset of call indices on the root path (grad k ::m repr(base k)). Together with vertex_eq_repr (planned: vertex = x0 - gamma * sum over repr), this is Def. 2.3.
Identifying a gradient by its call index (point and sample of that computation) is the accepted graph interpretation.

gradientOracle P g answers a query x at call k with g x (tape k), and the tape has law P. Instance (f, lower) is hidden from the algorithm. This is the stochastic-gradient access of the problem over R^d.
The oracle reveals only g(x; xi) values. f, lower and mu stay hidden.
EpsStationary f x P eps (integrable and E||grad f(x)||^2 <= eps) defines the notion. The public criterion writes the same inequality inline, with <= p.eps (no squaring).
Same convention as the source. The integrability conjunct is the accepted regularity.

Planned main_theorem has: all hypotheses (A1-A3 via SmoothObjective, LowerBounded, IsStochasticGradient and marginals hlaw; WellFormed and IsMainBranch; C1-C3), every natural K >= 4(R+1)L(f x0 - lower)/eps + 8 sigma^2 L(f x0 - lower)/eps^2, and the conclusion of integrability plus (1/K) sum_{k<K} E||grad f(x^{m k})||^2 <= eps with gamma = stepSize. This is Theorem 2.4 with the exact gap.

The conclusion is the accepted graph contract (integrability included). The source constants are unchanged, and the refined proof route is planned (descent_point keeps (gamma/2)(1 - L gamma), then young_split/assembly). The previous independent LP check supports plausibility. Lean 1/0 = 0 affects only K = 0, which forces a zero gap.

stepSize L sigma eps R = min(1/(2L), min(if R = 0 then 1/(2L) else 1/(2RL), if sigma = 0 then 1/(2L) else eps/(4 sigma^2 L))). Substituting 1/(2L) for an omitted term never lowers the min below the source value, so this equals the source min with the +infinity convention.
No change in any regime. stepSize_facts plans the proofs of L*gamma <= 1/2, L*gamma*R <= 1/2 and L*gamma*sigma^2 <= eps/4.
Tree with WellFormed (base j, point j, grad j <= j), and fold/foldHist for recursion over parents. Each node j+1 has the unique parent base j. This is the computation tree.
WellFormed expresses exactly "choose already computed points/gradients". Nothing else is added.

valid: 0 < L, 0 <= sigma, 0 < eps, 0 <= Delta, 0 <= R, plus the tree/branch conditions. These are the accepted graph domains. Delta >= 0 is implied by f x0 - lower <= Delta whenever an admissible instance exists.

The same stepSize L sigma eps R is used in publicInput (Public.gamma), in admissible (SampleIndependent) and in main_theorem. The same tree/branch/x0/g/P flow into vertex, the conditions and the output. Graph bindings are preserved.

Hypotheses are split between valid (conditions on the method: WellFormed, IsMainBranch, C2, C3) and admissible (A1-A3, C1, gap bound, oracle form). Both are premises of Convergence. Polarity and quantifiers (forall valid p, I, O) are preserved, and the conclusion is not assumed anywhere.
All seven assumption clauses occur once in the setup design. The only addition is the Delta upper-bound premise f x0 - lower <= p.Delta, which belongs to the adaptation (known input).
Horizon ceil(4(R+1)L Delta/eps + 8 sigma^2 L Delta/eps^2) and stepSize reproduce the source formulas. The budget lambda expands the same ceiling inside p.branch.

birch q has: Seed a uniform index in Fin(K+1); State (count, hist, chosen); query = node point(count); update = Hist.step; output = node branch(chosen). allowedAlgorithm A = birch q pins the method to Algorithm 1 on the supplied tree with the source step size.

The ambient law is the Convergence product of the uniform index law and the oracle tape law P. The tape has arbitrary dependence subject to marginals mu and Condition 1 (no IID imposed), which respects the source. The uniform index is independent of the samples, as the transport needs.
T is owned in Proofs as main_theorem. Its single public wrapper outputs.Theorems.BirchSgd.result owns no node.
repr is a multiset of call indices, and vertex_eq_repr is planned to connect it to point values.

Independently checked each field against the source. d (dimension), L and sigma (Assumptions 1.1/1.3 constants used in the source step size) are problem_data. eps is the accuracy. x0 is the Algorithm 1 input, a known_input. Delta is a known_input: the source horizon needs Delta = f(x^0) - f^*, which the algorithm cannot compute without f, so a supplied upper bound is the only legitimate public substitute, and admissible requires f x0 - lower <= Delta. tree and branch are family_setting: Theorem 2.4 is stated for "any SGD method represented by computation tree G" and a main branch of it, so the tree (with the fixed-structure interpretation) and its main branch identify the source method. They are constrained by valid (WellFormed, IsMainBranch, C2, C3) and drive the queries, updates and output, so they are not free horizons. R is the Condition 3 constant of the chosen method: it is checked by DistanceBounded in valid and enters gamma and K, a legitimate family setting or known bound. Derived quantities (gamma, K) are not Params fields: they are computed in publicInput from public fields via Algorithms.stepSize/horizon. No field encodes the conclusion.

The criterion is inline: Measurable output and Integrable ||gradient I.f (output)||^2 and integral of ||gradient I.f(output)||^2 dP <= p.eps. The source convention eps bounds the squared norm. The output is the implemented node branch(iota) of the realised tree with uniform iota in Fin(K+1). Its expectation under the product law equals the average over k <= K, which main_theorem bounds with K' = K+1 >= bound (planned via uniform_prefix_accuracy and execute_birch). There is no tuning or work premise inside successful.

Budget fun p _ => p.branch ceil(4(R+1)L Delta/eps + 8 sigma^2 L Delta/eps^2). One oracle = one framework step = one stochastic-gradient evaluation (the query at node point(count)). Node j+1 is created by call j, so exactly branch(K) calls create nodes 0..branch(K), and branch is strictly increasing. This is therefore the exact number of calls this method needs to produce x^0..x^K. It is a derived count (the source horizon composed with the method's structure map), not a free horizon. For Vanilla SGD, branch = id and it reduces to the source iteration count. The component uses the accuracy eps. The boundary cases (rounding, Delta = 0, R = 0, sigma = 0, calls versus iterations) are listed with planned proofs.

Kind derived, no approval needed. main_theorem keeps the exact source statement. The adaptation does three things. (i) It replaces the exact gap by the supplied upper bound Delta, which is valid because the source bound is monotone in Delta (all coefficients are nonnegative with L, eps > 0), so K' = ceil(bound(Delta)) + 1 >= bound(exact gap). (ii) It returns x^iota with iota uniform on {0..K}, independent of the tape, whose expectation is exactly the source average. (iii) It proves the execution correspondence. The method (tree, branch, step size) and all source cases are preserved.
Headline: K >= 4(R+1)L Delta/eps + 8 sigma^2 L Delta/eps^2 main-branch iterations, a natural number. It is kept separate from template calls, with the source units.

Execution is template_oracle_calls in Fin 1 -> N, equal to the design budget expression. The single component routes every query to oracle 0. Execution stops after branch(K) calls, and by then nodes 0..branch(K) exist.

The conversion is iterations K -> calls branch(K), with witnesses execute_birch (execute with budget branch K returns vertex(branch i) for i <= K) and branch_mono. The plan states honestly that the source gives no bound on branch(K) in terms of K. This is correct: the paper's headline is the iteration rate, and gradient counts or time are method-specific.
One setup with one consumer T in identical mode. shared_hypotheses equal T.result_context.hypotheses, and shared_parameters equal T.result_context.parameters. Nothing is strengthened or dropped.

notes: Cost model: each framework step issues one oracle call, even when its new edge reuses an earlier gradient (grad j < j). For methods with reuse such as Local SGD, the template count branch(K) can exceed the number of distinct gradient computations of the real method. This is an honest upper count of this formal algorithm's calls and is consistent with literal Algorithm 1. The source headline (main-branch iterations) is kept separately.
